steps.heading: The Psochic Hegemony
body: Judging ideas, concepts and people through relative morality.
This runs about 15 minutes. Nothing you enter identifies you.

steps.heading: A pre-knowledge test. How do you feel about the Psochic Hegemony Graph?
That was interesting
body: Some people have a natural inclination to liking or disliking the map on first impressions.
There's no need to be afraid, it's just a map of good and bad.

steps.heading: Calibration
body: To begin we must calibrate your understanding. Some people are able to feel the Psochic Hegemony, the Ruling Principle of the Mind, the Map of Good and Evil naturally — when they look at Greater Good and think Greater Evil, they'll feel a gradient or a discernable bodily feeling.

Most people cannot, since 'like' only interacts with 'like' and 'like' understands 'like'. Good and Evil can only be felt as strongly as one understands it. Your Body understands Good more than your Mind does; a starving person never says "good is an illusion" when being handed sustenance, as that is an example of Good. Similarly they'd never say "bad is an illusion" if you took the sustenance from their starving mouth and sold it to another. They would, however, if you gave them a rock and took it away.
In the following section, imagine you are and have been in a desert, you're starving and parched. Place each scenario where you feel it belongs. Do not overthink it. Yes, it's as simple as it seems.

steps.heading: You're starving and parched, I give you food and water
You're starving and parched, I sell you food and water
You're starving and parched, I take your food and water
You're starving and parched, I let you have my water
You're starving and parched, I give you a rock
You're starving and parched, I take your rock
You're starving and parched, I take your rock and sell it

tokens.label: take your rock and sell it

steps.heading: Calibration Recap
body: If you assume the rock has intrinsic value you may have placed it toward Good Preference when given, and toward Bad Preference or Lesser Evil when taken and sold — because the rock has assumed a value you missed, and was 'stolen' from you.

The Lesser Evil is the greed zone; in this context the Greater Evil is the effects of greed. From the perspective of Greed, taking the rock and selling it from under you is the Greater Evil, as that's opposite to what they wanted to do with it. If you recognize the rock still has no intrinsic value, you'd land near the centre — confusion as to why they took it at all.
We did not say 'Sulphur in the context of medicine', or 'Gemstone', 'metal', or even 'Ore'. Even a starving person in the desert can find a rock for themselves.

Note the reactions of the will axis. Having something sold from you, even something as worthless as sand in the desert, opposes your sense of fairness and generates will. Willpower is generated from a reaction of external events against one's worldview, determined by magnitude of opposition or support and justification.

A thing's objective worth comes from its objective benefit relative to completing a task. Survival is the one shared goal of all Life, so sustenance has universal benefit and universal understanding of benefit. The lesson is that periods of abundance mute the sense of suffering, and the understanding of Bad. This in turn mutes the sense of Good, and is easily achieved by overthinking.

steps.heading: The fruit basket experiment
body: Imagine two baskets of fruit. One is very good, full of the ripest fruit you love to eat. One is very bad, so bad they cannot be eaten — putrid, rotting, disgusting. Place them both.

Then try moving the good basket to the opposite side and listen to how wrong it feels. Keep it there and imagine time passing — what happens to it over months, over years? Then do the same with the bad basket. Then imagine the good basket on the good point, and someone stealing it and replacing it with poison.
steps.followUp: Describe how that felt — especially where it resisted you.

steps.heading: Recap
body: Bags of sand in the desert introduce a perceptual inversion: something that should be bad is good, what should be good is bad. Strength feels like Burden and Burden feels like Strength. The inner hegemony is the perception from the self — this is why people vote against their interests and are comfortable permitting systemic evils.
What follows is organized into topics rather than one long line. If a scenario feels like it sits at a perceived point rather than a true one, place it there — the inner ring is marked.

steps.heading: Choose a topic
body: Each topic is a short set of scenarios on the same map. Do them in any order — you'll come back here between topics — and use Review & Submit once you've covered what you want to cover.
